Same here. Can confirm this is still happening on 1.18.29.

OS: Artix Linux x86_64 (KDE Wayland)
CPU: i7-10610U
Process: opencode TUI (cwd=$HOME)

Sits at ~100%+ CPU on a single core doing completely nothing.

% time     seconds  usecs/call     calls    errors syscall
57.06    9.859336         188     52375      2515 futex
25.93    4.480677       16473       272           epoll_pwait2
13.36    2.307910          40     57374           sched_yield
3.30    0.569416       43801        13         4 restart_syscall

Tried disabling fff with OPENCODE_DISABLE_FFF=1 (verified in env) and it made zero difference. $HOME isn't a git repo either so it's not the git status polling issue (#21699). No child processes running, 41 FDs open, just sitting idle on an established connection.

Looks like a tight busy-wait loop in the event bus / SDK layer. epoll_pwait2 immediately returns ready and spins sched_yield ~7k times/sec instead of actually sleeping. Bun's GC (HeapHelper) constantly sits at ~40% combined CPU just trying to keep up with the allocations from whatever loop is running.

The first half of this issue is fixed by **PR #47542** — [fix(opencode): sanitize MCP tool schemas for Anthropic root combinators](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/47542).

### What it covers (matches your repro exactly)

The PR adds a targeted `sanitizeAnthropicSchema` alongside the existing OpenAI branch (#32489):
- Detects the Anthropic family via the AI SDK adapter: `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, `@ai-sdk/google-vertex/anthropic`, and `@ai-sdk/github-copilot` **only when it proxies a Claude model** (it also proxies GPT models, which must stay on the OpenAI path).
- Folds root-level `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` into the root object schema:
  - `allOf` (an intersection): member `properties` merged and `required` unioned.
  - `anyOf`/`oneOf` (exclusive alternatives Anthropic can't represent): dropped so the root object stays valid without being over-constrained.
  - Nested combinators inside `properties` are preserved verbatim (Anthropic allows those).

This directly covers your `pick_one` repro (root `anyOf: [{required:["a"]},{required:["b"]}]`) and the `ai-memory` server case, plus the `github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5` provider you hit.

### Still open

The **second, separable half** remains: MCP tool definitions never reach the `tool.definition` hook, so plugins can't work around provider quirks without proxying the MCP server. That's independent of the sanitizer above and is not addressed by #47542 — it's worth tracking separately (your reproduction shows built-ins fire the hook while MCP tools skip the tool-assembly path).

Can reproduce on Linux (WSL2) with `opencode web --hostname 0.0.0.0` started with cwd `/` — project `global` has `worktree: "/"`.

Confirmed server-side: `GET /session?directory=/&roots=true&limit=55` **and** `GET /api/session` both return the session; it renders fine when opened via deep link (`open-project?directory=/` even issues the correct request — the item is still filtered out of the list).

Two additional data points:
- The one property that differs between hidden and visible sessions in the same project is `subpath`: hidden = root session with empty `path`/`subpath`, visible = non-empty `subpath` (e.g. `home/ssa`). Suggests the list filter drops `subpath === ""`.
- `PATCH /session/:id {"directory": "/home/ssa"}` returns 200 and echoes the session but does not persist — legacy root sessions cannot be migrated into a visible project at all.

Related: #42627 (desktop remote server), and note that Windows desktop clients send their own cwd as project directory to a Linux server (`C:\\temp` was stored server-side as `/home/ssa/C:\\temp`), which compounds the visibility problem.

Reproducing on Windows Desktop against a WSL2 server (`opencode web --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 4096`, v1.18.29). The desktop registers the project as `\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\ssa` (UNC path from the native Windows file picker), and every list query uses that string — while `session.directory` on the server is `/home/ssa`. The server happily resolves the foreign hint against its own cwd: it previously stored `directory=C:\temp` as `/home/ssa/C:\temp` — the exact unmerged issue #34255 (PRs #34256/#40857 still open) — so the desktop's read key never matches the write key; same "normalised on write, exact-match on read" asymmetry described in #44216.
Sessions render perfectly via deep link (which bypasses the Home directory filter), confirming server state is healthy. The `--mdns --mdns-domain` workaround from #19473 avoids UNC entirely and may be worth documenting for WSL users. What do maintainers consider the right layer to fix: rejecting foreign hints server-side (#40857), or making the desktop adopt the server-reported project path after connect?
